newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israel and China sign pact on maritime trade.
newsitem.headline: Israel and China sign pact on maritime trade.

text.p: Israel and China on Sunday signed an agreement granting each other most-favoured nation (MFN) status on maritime issues, Israel's Foreign Ministry said.
The agreement was signed by Israeli Foreign Minister David Levy and Chinese Transport Minister Huang Zhendong, who is leading a delegation of Chinese state-owned shipping company officials to Israel.

The agreement grants MFN status to the two sides in matters of access to ports, payment of taxes and fees, the use of port facilities, unloading and other matters, the ministry said. It also allows port authorities and shipping companies to set up representative offices in the opposite country.

The ministry said the agreement was important for Zim Israel Navigation, Israel's biggest shipping company, which had had difficulty operating in China. Zim will no longer need to get advance permission to dock in Chinese ports or rely on Chinese agents to handle it operations there, it said.
Zim is controlled by the Israeli government and Israel Corp.
